$$ \text{Vehicles on Day 1} = 2 \text{ containers} \times 5 \text{ vehicles/container} = 10 \text{ vehicles} $$

**Step 2: Determine the total number of vehicles imported on the second day.**

$$ \text{Vehicles on Day 2} = \text{Total Vehicles} - \text{Vehicles on Day 1} $$
$$ \text{Vehicles on Day 2} = 30 - 10 = 20 \text{ vehicles} $$

**Step 3: Calculate the number of containers imported on the second day.**
The problem states that all containers contain 5 vehicles each. To find the number of containers brought in on the second day, we divide the number of vehicles added on the second day by the number of vehicles per container.
$$ \text{Containers on Day 2} = \frac{\text{Vehicles on Day 2}}{\text{Vehicles per container}} $$
$$ \text{Containers on Day 2} = \frac{20}{5} = 4 \text{ containers} $$

There were 4 containers imported on the second day.
